label: Payments and financial messaging
summary: Card-brand and network schemes where an outside party sets the level and the proof: the acquirer or card brand decides how a merchant validates (PCI DSS), and SWIFT requires every user to declare an architecture type and attest each year (CSCF).

requires_org.reason: Payment card data (or SWIFT messages) must be listed with where it lives.
Payment third parties and service bureaus are part of the scope.
Account data flows are the basis of PCI scope.

source.ref: PCI DSS v4.0.1 and PCI SSC SAQ documents; card-brand merchant and service-provider levels; acquirers and brands decide who validates and how

fields.label: Entity role
fields.note: Merchants and service providers have different levels and different SAQs; a service provider can only use SAQ D for service providers.

fields.label: Card brands
fields.note: Each brand sets its own levels and thresholds.

fields.label: Acquirer
fields.note: The acquiring bank. It, or the brand, confirms the level and how the merchant validates.

fields.label: Yearly transactions
fields.note: Largest single-brand yearly count. Visa Level 1 starts above 6 million transactions; Level 2 is 1 to 6 million; Level 3 is 20,000 to 1 million e-commerce.

fields.label: Level
fields.note: Set by the brand and the acquirer, not by the organisation. Not assigned yet blocks the gate until written confirmation arrives.

fields.label: Level confirmed
fields.note: The acquirer or brand has confirmed the level, validation route and deadline in writing.

fields.label: Validation route
options: Report on Compliance by a QSA
Report on Compliance by an ISA
fields.note: A QSA or an internal security assessor writes a Report on Compliance; smaller merchants use a self-assessment questionnaire. Always confirm with the acquirer.

fields.label: SAQ type
fields.note: A: card-not-present, everything outsourced. A-EP: e-commerce where the merchant site controls redirection. B: imprint or dial-out terminals. B-IP: standalone IP terminals. C-VT: manual keying into a third-party virtual terminal. C: payment application connected to the internet. P2PE: listed P2PE only. SPoC: phone with a secure card reader. D: everyone else.

fields.label: QSA or ISA

in: Report on Compliance by a QSA
Report on Compliance by an ISA

fields.note: Name of the assessor firm or the internal assessor. ISAs exist at sponsor companies only.

fields.label: ASV vendor
fields.note: Approved scanning vendor for the quarterly external vulnerability scans. A QSA cannot replace them.

fields.label: Approach
fields.note: The customised approach is for risk-mature entities, needs targeted risk analyses and may be limited by acquirers or brands.

fields.label: AOC signatory
fields.note: Signs the Attestation of Compliance. Only PCI SSC forms are accepted.

source.ref: PCI DSS v4.0.1 section 4 and requirements 1.2.4, 12.5.1, 12.5.2: account data flows, CDE and connected-to systems, annual scope confirmation, segmentation testing

fields.label: Payment channels
fields.note: Every channel through which account data enters or leaves.

fields.label: PAN storage
fields.note: Whether the card number is stored. Unknown means a data discovery has to run first, including logs and dumps.

fields.label: Data flow diagram
fields.note: Account data flows are drawn and kept current; requirement 1.2.4 and 12.5.2 ask for it annually.

fields.label: CDE systems
fields.note: Systems that store, process or transmit account data, plus connected-to and security-impacting systems (authentication, logging, DNS, remote access).

fields.label: CDE sites
fields.note: Sites where card data is handled.

fields.label: Segmentation
options: Segmented, to be validated by penetration test
Not segmented: whole network in scope
fields.note: Segmentation is not required, but without it the whole network is in scope. It must be validated by penetration testing.

fields.label: Segmentation test

when.eq: Segmented, to be validated by penetration test

fields.note: Planned date of the segmentation penetration test.

fields.label: Payment providers
fields.note: Third-party service providers with access to account data or that can affect its security. A compliant provider does not make the entity compliant.

fields.label: Responsibility matrix
fields.note: Who owns which requirement between the entity and each provider (requirement 12.8 and 12.9).

source.ref: PCI DSS v4.0.1 section 12: annual scope confirmation by the entity, ROC or SAQ plus AOC, quarterly ASV scans

fields.label: Scope confirmed by
fields.note: The entity confirms scope itself every year (every six months for service providers); the assessor's confirmation does not replace it.

fields.label: AOC target
fields.note: The date by which the AOC must reach the acquirer or brand.

fields.label: First scan
fields.note: Date of the first quarterly ASV scan.

source.ref: SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework: architecture types A1, A2, A3, A4 and B decide the applicable controls (swift.com was unreachable; read in consultancy guides)

fields.label: Architecture type
fields.note: A1: you own the communication and messaging interfaces. A2: you own the messaging interface only. A3: a SWIFT-supplied connector for app-to-app. A4: your own connector. B: no local SWIFT infrastructure. A wrong type means the wrong controls.

fields.label: Environments
fields.note: Declare for every environment and take the most encompassing type.

fields.label: Components
fields.note: What sits in the secure zone. Provider-hosted components can still be in your scope.

fields.label: BICs
fields.note: Business identifier codes the attestation covers and who owns the infrastructure behind each. Many users do not know this.

fields.label: Service bureau
fields.note: Name of the service bureau, if any. Ask it what is inside your scope.

source.ref: SWIFT KYC-SA annual attestation by 31 December; independent assessment, internal or external (consultancy guides; swift.com unreachable)

fields.label: Assessment type
fields.note: The assessor must be independent of the people who run the controls.

fields.label: Assessor
fields.note: Person or firm. Internal assessors need recent assessment experience and a relevant certification such as CISA, CISSP or CISM.

fields.label: Assessor independent
fields.note: Confirms the assessor is outside the first line.

fields.label: Attestation signatory
fields.note: Management signs the attestation in KYC-SA. Attest by 31 December each year.

fields.label: Last assessment
fields.note: Prior findings can sometimes be reused if the last assessment ended under two years ago and nothing relevant changed (reported by consultancies; confirm with SWIFT).

gate.label: The acquirer or brand has confirmed the level in writing
gate.hint: Ask the acquirer for the level, route and deadline in writing.

gate.label: A level has been assigned
gate.hint: Choose the level the acquirer gave.

gate.label: The validation route is known
gate.hint: ROC or SAQ, as the acquirer states.

gate.label: The segmentation decision is made
gate.hint: Segmented with a test plan, or the whole network is in scope.

gate.label: It is known whether card numbers are stored
gate.hint: Run a PAN discovery before relying on the scope.

gate.label: The SWIFT assessor is independent
gate.hint: The assessor cannot be the first line.
